business_rules.statement: The Statement of Work fixes the command channel at five classes and names them in a table with their origins; a command channel with an open class list is a remote-execution surface.
On authority-check fail, the command never enters the channel and the attempt is audited — an unauthorised command never becomes a queued object at all.
Only after the device acknowledges may a surface state that the command took effect on that device.
Where a later command supersedes an unapplied one, exactly one applies.
Every state transition that changes a record writes its audit row in the same transaction.
Lot release is refused for every role except Quality Manager, on every instance in the class, with no exception by work type, risk class, or tag.
business_rules.enforcement_point: authorization check on lot release class

business_rules.statement: A version-change command never takes effect inside a run in flight.
business_rules.enforcement_point: device version application, staged for next execution boundary

business_rules.statement: The compliance-suspension device message is exactly "Operation suspended. Contact your supervisor. Your work has been saved."
Every command instance carries a value for all thirty-one attributes.
An instance whose authority does not match its class is refused registration and cannot be created.
business_rules.enforcement_point: class-level authority check before the channel

business_rules.statement: The channel set is closed at two — in-app and email — platform-wide, at every tier. In-app notifications cannot be muted.
business_rules.enforcement_point: notification delivery adapters and both configuration levels

business_rules.statement: A notification must never be the only mechanism enforcing safety, a hold, qualification, authorization, approval, suspension, or a device command.
business_rules.enforcement_point: enforcement lives on device/package/lifecycle state/command channel

business_rules.statement: Where nobody holds the target role, delivery falls back to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, explicitly marked as a fallback delivery.

Exactly six integration paths exist at V1: two single sign-on protocols, the platform-managed credential path, the email vendor, bundled artificial-intelligence compute, and the enterprise-resource-planning scaffolding.
The costed-V2 rule: if a single integration becomes commercially required to land a launch tenant, it is scoped as a costed V2 addition — one named, read-only inbound target — not pulled into V1.
No surface displays an action as completed on command creation or authorisation; completion requires device acknowledgement.
No surface displays "synced", "done", "complete", or any equivalent single word as the sole state of a capture or command.
business_rules.enforcement_point: string audit on all five surfaces

business_rules.statement: Every hold displays as issued, propagating, or in force per device, with each device named and its last-seen time available.
No agent writes an operational record without a human gate or pre-authorised, Studio-authored policy approved at publication.
No agent classifies a deviation; deterministic logic owns classification, on-device, at the instant of capture.
No agent releases a Severity 1 hold under any circumstance.
No number a supervisor may have acted on is silently rewritten; a material recompute is itself an audited event.
An unaudited change is impossible; the change and its audit row commit together.
Quarantined and rejected data is retained and visible, never discarded.
An action and its audit event commit in the same transaction — an action that cannot be audited does not happen.
Commands travel down the command channel and apply at the device's next sync, in order; there is no real-time remote control of a worker mid-run.
A tenant may make the platform stricter than default and may never make it looser than the platform floor; the platform rejects a looser-than-floor value at the point of entry rather than logging it.
business_rules.enforcement_point: platform floor register at point of entry

business_rules.statement: Onboarding is invitation-driven; there is no public self-signup at V1.
The implementation authoring role is author-and-submit only, never approve or release, fully audited, and revoked at the end of onboarding.
No tenant becomes reachable before its isolated data space is confirmed provisioned.
Exactly one Tenant Admin is seeded per tenant by the platform side; thereafter user management is tenant-administered.
A looser-than-floor value is rejected at entry with the bound stated and is not persisted.
A package-borne configuration change is never displayed as in force on a device before that device confirms the package version.
The hierarchy is Site to Area (Line) to Location (Cell) to Job to Run, and it is a platform-wide data-model contract no surface may fork.
Job Owner is a field, not a role. The Job state machine is draft to pending_approval to active to archived, and segregation of duties is absolute: the creator of a Job cannot approve that same Job.
Archiving an Area auto-pauses every bound Job, notifies the Tenant Admin with the list, and prompts reassignment before archival completes.
An Area with no bound Shift cannot receive a Job.
Editing a Shift does not re-stamp completed runs.
A missed digest is recorded as missed, never as empty.
Worker-Shift counting attributes one unit per worker per calendar shift regardless of run count, and one to each worker who actually worked where a substitution occurred.
The creator of a Job can never approve that Job, including where the creator holds the approver role.
A Job cannot reach active while referencing an unpublished workflow version.
A Service Type tag pre-populates but never fixes qualification requirements — the tag suggests, never decides.
No worker may enter, edit, or attest their own qualification.
The four warning stages at 14, 7, 1, and 0 days cannot be removed or delayed by any tenant setting.
A qualification state change reaches a device only over the command channel and is reported per device, never as an instant global truth.
Under the strict posture a worker completes the current run and is blocked from the next assignment requiring the expired certification.
Attribution follows the login, never the device.
The cached-credential window cannot exceed 72 hours under any tenant setting.
The last Tenant Admin cannot be removed; the last approver-capable user cannot be removed while a Job exists.
No custom role can be created at V1, and no Quality Director role exists.
Scope values may never cross tenants; cross-tenant data isolation is platform-fixed.
A recertification expiry must postdate the previous expiry.
A second clearance in the same Area on the same shift routes to the Quality Manager irrespective of which worker it concerns.
Devices below the app-version floor cannot enroll; mode is fixed at enrollment.
Reassignment is refused while a run is in flight on the device; eviction follows confirmed receipt plus integrity check, never an attempted upload.
A lost report never triggers an automatic erasure.
Wipe requires root approval as a critical-class action; a final sync is attempted before erasure whenever the device is reachable.
A partially drained queue halts the wipe pending an explicit decision.

No Workflow content reaches the frontline without explicit human sign-off at each of three stages — Author, Reviewer, Release Authority; the Reviewer must differ from the Author, no role performs two stages on one submission, the Reviewer cannot edit content directly, and the Release Authority cannot be bypassed.
Every republish requires a mandatory description that doubles as the worker-facing change notice on the first screen of the next execution.
business_rules.enforcement_point: republish form and Frontline first screen

business_rules.statement: Each run pins its package at assignment and the pin is immutable for the life of the run.
Every measurement screen carries at least one severity mapping before submission; specification limits require lower limit, upper limit, unit, and drawing reference.
No published version can be edited in place; a republish description is mandatory for every class; a mis-classified patch is returned rather than published.
A version with no generated package cannot be adopted by a Job.
The worker-facing change notice text equals the mandatory republish description.
Training Library content is never packaged; escalation delivery is server-side and not packaged.
A run cannot be assigned without a pinnable package.
No published version is ever deleted or hidden; a rollback passes the full three-stage chain and publishes as a new higher version.

All assignment is supervisor-driven at V1; worker self-assignment is deferred. There is no availability or double-booking check beyond the qualification check at V1, and concurrency is unlimited with step attribution by individual identity.

Sync is continuous when connected, resumes automatically on reconnection, and is never a worker action; the upload queue is durable and resumable, and a manual sync control exists only as a convenience, never a dependency.

Captured media stays in the Frontline application's encrypted store and never touches the device gallery. Evidence is immutable at creation; corrections are append-only annotation records carrying who, when, and what changed.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Frontline capture store and every surface

business_rules.statement: Every capture carries both device time and server-receipt time, with server receipt authoritative for ordering.
A device holds only what its assigned runs require; interrupted downloads resume rather than restart; eviction follows complete-and-synced with an integrity check.
No worker may override a gate on the device; coaching absence never unblocks a gate.
A Severity 1 hold is placed locally and immediately, offline.
Evidence is immutable at creation on every surface; a quarantined capture is neither accepted nor discarded; an unsynced capture is never displayed as recorded.
No notice interrupts an in-flight run; execution on a notified-class version cannot begin without its notice.

No artificial-intelligence model sits in the deviation-triggering path. Detection is rule-based and runs on the worker's device using the version-pinned package; agents activate only after a deterministic trigger.

The Severity 1 floor is automatic lot freeze plus Quality-Manager-only release plus escalation, platform-fixed. Where the freeze lands: the Lot where a lot exists, the Unit where work is serialized, otherwise the Run.
A missing deviation form blocks the gate rather than the record — an unrecorded deviation must never be traded for continued production.
An unclassifiable out-of-specification value gates the step and is never treated as acceptable.
A missing containment checklist is recorded as an evidence gap, never silently skipped.
An anomaly cannot be resolved without a closure note; reclassification requires a recorded reason.
No device resumes work on a held lot before applying the release.

Lane A is everything that does not alter a configured operating value — applied automatically, logged, reversible, tenant-visible. Lane B is everything that does — never auto-approved, decided by a Quality Manager and above.
Every Lane A refinement is logged before it is applied; an unlogged refinement must not be applied.
Undecided Lane B proposals age with a 30-day stale flag and never expire silently, because expiry would erase the evidence of a decision not taken.
Shift-handoff acknowledgement is distinct from opening and never blocks shift start; a missing brief is flagged, never rendered as empty.
Every report carries a data-as-of timestamp; material corrections are flagged in the next delivery; a missed delivery is recorded as missed.
No notification is the sole enforcement of any control.
The audit log is append-only and immutable on every path; an interrupted export produces no file; tamper-evidence is not claimed at V1.

no expiry for version change; a stale notice is harmless

contradictions.description: Device wipe and de-authorisation reaches a device but is not one of the five named command-channel classes; §7.2.2 fixes five classes while §7.11 and §8.13.3 require a remote wipe instruction to reach a device.
CMD-SUSP-005 device wipe is listed in the suspension-class panel yet marked `Client Decision Required — reaches the device but is not one of the five named classes`.
conflicting_values: not one of the five named classes

contradictions.description: Sync-then-wipe requires a final sync attempt before erasure, which an offline device cannot perform; no bound is stated for a device that never returns.
conflicting_values: wipe blocks on the sync attempt

contradictions.description: 27.3 Command lifecycle is described as a fourteen-state enumeration in the classification table while 27.9 Rule 1 and 28.1 both enumerate fifteen command states.
Job location binding: §4.5.1 states one Area per Job is a hard constraint; §2.1 supersedes it with one parent node per Job at the tenant's configured depth.
conflicting_values: one parent node per Job at configured depth (§2.1)

contradictions.description: Site level: §2.1 marks Site-as-required-minimum an open drafting recommendation while §4.3.1 states the Site level is mandatory.
Record-finish window bounds: §2.4 marks the bounds open at drafting while §4.6.8 and §8.19 state them as settled.

Quality Director role: §6.1.3 lists Plant Manager and Quality Director as a Command Center user group and §5.18 lists Plant Manager under Fixed role, while §3.5 states five roles and denies the Quality Director.
conflicting_values: Quality Director exists as a user group (§6.1.3)

contradictions.description: Approval chain versus Lane B auto-publish: §5.11.1 requires human sign-off at each of three stages while §5.16.3 and §6.7.4 have an approved Lane B proposal auto-publish a patch with no second approval.
Library pointers versus pinning: §5.7 says screens hold pointers and a library edit propagates immediately, while §5.14 and Part II say a run's package is pinned and never re-based.
conflicting_values: pinned and never re-based (§5.14, Part II)

contradictions.description: Capture-type set: §1.7 and §7.8.3 name measurement, scan, photo, checklist, boolean, e-signature and free text while §5.5.3 names measurement entry, photo capture, barcode/QR scan, checkbox confirmation, digital signature, free text and dropdown selection.
Difficulty-level packaging: §5.9 leaves open whether the package carries all three difficulty levels or only the assigned worker's.
Package-borne versus server-only field assignment: §6.7.4 says Part VII carries the authoritative field-by-field assignment and Part VII does not enumerate it.
conflicting_values: Part VII does not enumerate it

contradictions.description: Prevention Agent gating: §3.7 and §6.6.1 place it under pre-authorised Studio-authored policy with a runtime gate only for beyond-policy proposals, while §8.3.2 and §8.3.3 say every action agent routes through a human gate and label it action-gated.
Report set 4 identity: §4.10.5 names it "Clearance (qualification-override) frequency by role" while §6.12.1 names it "Override frequency by role".
Reconnection ordering: the Statement of Work never fixes whether a reconnecting device uploads pending captures before or after pulling pending commands.

failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The draft stays in review and nothing publishes
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A working diff

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The preview renderer fails on a screen type
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry the preview
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The submission stays in review; nothing advances unreviewed
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A working preview

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Version creation succeeds but package generation fails
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry package generation
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Version marked published-not-distributable; the prior version remains in force on every device
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Successful package generation

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The notification to the Author fails after a rejection
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-send the notification
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The submission stays in draft with its comments attached; nothing publishes
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The Author revising (WF-AUT-007); the queue shows returned items regardless

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The Author resubmits without addressing a comment
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The Reviewer returns again with sharper comments
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The draft remains unpublished; the floor keeps running the prior version
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A successful advance

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Distribution partially completes: some devices hold the new version, others the old
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Redistribute to devices that have not confirmed
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Mixed versions in the fleet, each device's version stated explicitly, and no claim that the floor is uniform
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Completing distribution; Supervisor on-demand re-pull

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Coaching assets exceed available device storage
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Regenerate the package
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No package, therefore no assignment to a device — a run cannot be assigned without a pinnable package
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Regeneration and re-pull; deliver without optional coaching assets with the omission recorded

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The pin is written but the package download fails
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry download
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The run stays assigned-not-ready and cannot start
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A completed download; Supervisor on-demand re-pull

failures_fallbacks.trigger: In-flight runs are executing a defective published version
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Publish the corrected version through the chain
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Runs already in flight cannot be re-based
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The defective version remains published and readable, no new runs are assigned to it, and in-flight runs are supervised to completion or cancelled — never silently re-based
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Fleet adoption of the corrected version; enumerate every run executed against the withdrawn version

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Assignment commits but the package pin fails
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry the pin and the delivery
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The run remains unassigned or assigned-not-ready; unstarted run alerts at +15 minutes and auto-cancels at +30 minutes
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Completed pin and delivery; assign a different qualified worker

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Package download is interrupted partway
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Resume the interrupted transfer
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The run is listed as not ready with the reason; the worker takes another assigned run
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A completed download; Supervisor on-demand re-pull

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Connectivity drops mid-screen or the coaching card is unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Continue on the authored Work Instructions
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The run is parked or handed back with its state preserved; a gate never opens because guidance was missing
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Continued execution; capture-ledger comparison at run close

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Offline period exceeds the credential-trust window
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Continue offline on the pinned package
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Work stops when the credential-trust window expires, with all local data preserved and a forced sync required
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reconnection (WF-RES-001); last-write-wins by device timestamp under the clock-skew guard

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Capture upload is interrupted or validation fails
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Resume the upload
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The capture remains committed locally and unsynced, visibly counted, and never presented as recorded
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Upload completion; corrections are append-only annotations; audited-recompute after run finish

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Change-notice text fails to load from the version record
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-fetch the notice from the package
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The worker runs a version whose notice they have seen; no execution begins on a notified-class version whose notice could not be shown
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A successful notice render

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The deviation capture form is missing from the package
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-render the form from the package
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The step is blocked, the run cannot advance past the gate, and the worker raises a hand-back flag
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Form availability; compare device-created deviations against server-mirrored deviations

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The package's severity mappings are absent or unparsable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-read the mapping from the package
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The step is blocked pending a re-pull of the package; an unclassifiable out-of-specification value is never treated as acceptable
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A valid mapping

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A sibling device stays offline for hours, so the hold never reaches in force
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-queue the propagation command at each sibling sync
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The breach point is frozen locally, the rest of the floor is named as not yet confirmed, and the platform never claims a fleet-wide freeze it has not achieved
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Full propagation; Supervisor physically quarantines material under the tenant's own process, recorded as a containment item

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The containment checklist is missing from the package
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-render from the package
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The deviation exists, the material is held where Severity 1 applied, and the gap is visible to the reviewing Quality Manager rather than absent
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Checklist availability; worker follows authored Work Instructions and raises a hand-back flag

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The tenant's quality system expects a formal corrective-and-preventive-action record the platform does not have
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Record the full narrative in the closure note
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Closure note insufficient for the tenant's process
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The anomaly remains Open, visible, and aging in the register and the digest, rather than being closed without evidence of resolution
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Resolution with a note; the tenant references the anomaly identifier from its own quality system

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The release command cannot reach an offline device holding the frozen lot
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-queue delivery at each device sync
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The lot stays frozen on any device that has not received the release, and the Client Command Center names those devices
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Full command delivery; Supervisor moves work to an unaffected lot or reassigns the run

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The Lane A refinement log write fails
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry the log write before applying
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Selection reverts to configured defaults — curated coaching defaults and straightforward similarity retrieval, exactly as at cold start
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A working log; revert any weight with no corresponding entry

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The auto-publish pipeline fails after a human approval
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry the patch publication
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The configured value the human set remains in force everywhere until a version carrying the new value is confirmed on each device
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Publication and distribution; change recorded as approved-not-published with the Quality Manager notified

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The Shift Handoff Agent fails and no brief is produced
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-run the brief generation
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Generation fails again; a second consecutive failure or a failure outlasting a shift escalates
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No brief, an honest flag, and the shift starts anyway
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A produced brief; the incoming lead reads the live board, feed and deviation workspace directly

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Report generation fails at the scheduled time
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Regenerate and deliver late, marked late with its intended time
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No file is delivered and a missed-delivery record exists; a report is never delivered with a fabricated or absent as-of stamp
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Delivery; on-demand generation from the screen

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The email provider rejects the message
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry on the failed channel
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The escalation never resolves to no one, the fallback is visibly marked, and the underlying enforcement is already in force independently of any message
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Delivery or escalation; escalate on timeout to the next tier per Studio-authored routing

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The requested audit export range is too large to generate inside a session
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Narrow the filter and retry
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No partial file is delivered as if complete; an interrupted export produces no file rather than a truncated one
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Request the export in segments by date range

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A command class acquires an instance that does not share the class's authority rules
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Authority is checked at the class level before the channel, so an instance cannot carry weaker authority than its class
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: An instance registered with its own authority rule
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: An instance whose authority does not match its class is refused registration and cannot be created
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Correction of the instance definition; every command created under the incorrect rule reversed by a compensating action decided by the Quality Manager

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The email vendor degrades
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: In-app delivery, which continues and cannot be muted, so no recipient loses every channel
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Both channels failing during a platform-wide incident
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The enforcement the notification accompanies is unaffected, and the undelivered state is visible rather than displayed as sent
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Vendor recovery and queued delivery; re-notification of unacknowledged Critical items at 4 hours (1 hour in Regulated-Industry mode)

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Scope creep at the boundary: a launch tenant's requirement pulling an integration into V1
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The costed-V2 rule applied literally — one target, named, read-only
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A second target added under the same rule
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The second target is refused and scoped separately, because the rule says one
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-scoping

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An honesty defect reaching production
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The eighteen tests run as release gates
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A defect that passes the tests because the tests were written against the same misunderstanding as the code
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The independent honesty audit executed by someone who did not write either the code or the tests
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Correction of the display and re-running the audit; every operational decision taken while a false completion state was displayed must be identified and reviewed

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A qualification state that is true on the server and false on a device, or the reverse
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-queue the command and re-attempt at next sync
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The device continues under its cached qualification state within the trust window; beyond the window cached state is no longer trusted and a forced sync is required
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The run parks at the gate and the worker continues other assigned runs
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The clearance or recertification landing at sync; clearance corpus queryable from the Super Admin platform console

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The identity provider is unreachable or rejects
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The platform-managed credential path, the same mechanism as the worker personal identification number
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Access is refused; no session is created. The Frontline application continues offline under cached credentials within the trust window
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Identity provider restoration

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Credential store unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Cached credentials on the Frontline application within the trust window, default approximately 24 hours, ceiling 72 hours
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Designated high-risk actions requiring a forced sync are refused; the worker may continue lower-risk assigned work until the window closes, then access is refused
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Credential store restoration

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Compute unavailable, or an agent fails its evaluation gate
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Agent unavailability is rendered explicitly, never as silence
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The deterministic backbone continues untouched: gates, specification checks, severity classification, and the Severity 1 hold all operate, because the deterministic layer has no off switch
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Compute restoration; resume from an emergency pause is a separate audited act

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The stubbed endpoint is called
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: It returns 501, which is the correct and intended behaviour, not a fault
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not applicable — a stub that returns its designed response has not failed
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No run is created from an inbound call at V1; the enum value `erp_inbound` is never written
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Not applicable at V1

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A missing or duplicated workflow identifier
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: A duplicate identifier is resolved by retaining the earlier assignment and re-issuing the later one
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Two chapters have already published conflicting meanings for one identifier; both readings preserved and a DEC-* raised
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The identifier is marked disputed in the traceability index, and no test or acceptance criterion may reference a disputed identifier
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The decision is taken and the identifier re-issued; the traceability index regenerated
